<description>
Currently importing a descriptor to a wallet that has private keys requires the descriptor to include the private keys. This is not ideal as it means exposing private key material. This PR makes it so that the wallet will lookup and substitute the private keys for their respective public keys in such descriptors, thus enabling importing of public descriptors into wallets with private keys.

The underlying mechanism is that the wallet retrieves all of the pubkeys from the descriptor and checks to see if any of them have private keys in any `ScriptPubKeyMan`. Additionally, if the descriptor has a xpub with key origin info, we will check if any xprvs known to the wallet have a matching fingerprint and derive to the specified xpub. If so, the origin + xpub are replaced with the single xprv with the origin derivation path prepended to the key expression's derivation path.

Possible future work is to allow the xpub substitution to work when the wallet has some child in the key origin, i.e. the wallet xprv has a key origin that is a prefix of the key origin specified for an xpub in the descriptor. Currently this kind of substitution is not being done, only root master xprvs will be substituted.

If a wallet does not have the private keys for a public descriptor, the import is still disallowed.

This PR is based on #34861 to avoid an annoying rebase.

Closes #27336
</description>

[2026-10-22] c:6336446184 comment by fametrano (contributor) (edited 2026-10-22):
Tested b58383aca6: with the master key in the wallet, re-importing a descriptor the wallet already holds adds a duplicate.

I computed 20 vectors with a separate BIP32 implementation and imported them on regtest. They cover hardened, unhardened and mixed origins, the master as origin, a wrong fingerprint, the right fingerprint with a wrong path, `<0;1>`, hardened steps after the xpub, `tr()` script paths and `wsh(multi)` with a foreign key. 19 succeed or fail as expected, and their substituted descriptors derive the addresses I computed. The 20th led to the case below.

A wallet imports `wpkh([fpM/84h/1h/0h]xprvA/0/*)`, then `pkh(xprvM/0/*)`. Importing that `wpkh` again, public or private, stores `wpkh(xprvM/84h/1h/0h/0/*)`. Its descriptor ID is new, so `listdescriptors` lists the same public descriptor twice. With the master imported first, the first private `wpkh` import is already stored that way. Either way the private export carries the master key where the user gave an account key. Matching the wallet's exact xpub before the master would avoid the duplicate. Keeping the origin with the derived xprv would also keep the descriptor as given. The IWYU failure is this PR's: the new `KeyFingerprint` comparison needs `#include <array>` in `descriptor.cpp`. The vectors and script are available.
</new_statements>
